---
title: "CRS Inspector & Converter"
date: 2026-09-06
categories: [tool, geometry]
description: "Upload a GeoJSON or a Shapefile, find its coordinate reference system, spot a CRS that doesn't match its own coordinates, and convert to a different CRS. Free, runs entirely in your browser: the file never leaves your computer."
page-layout: full
---

Upload a file — `.geojson`, or a shapefile as a single `.zip` or as
`.shp`/`.dbf`/`.shx` selected together — and find out what coordinate
reference system it's actually in, whether that CRS is consistent with
its own coordinates, and convert it to a different one if you need to.

::: {.callout-tip}
**Private by design.** Your file is processed entirely in your
browser (Python via WebAssembly) — it's never uploaded to any server,
including ours. Nothing to configure, nothing to trust: the code
never gets the chance to see your data.
:::

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| output: false
// No fallback on page load (same reasoning as every other tool's own
// history) — the page starts genuinely empty until the user either
// uploads a file or clicks "Load example" below. Deliberately
// mismatched: no CRS is declared (GeoJSON has none), so it's read as
// WGS84 by default (per spec) — but the coordinates themselves are in
// the hundreds of thousands, Web Mercator magnitude. That mismatch IS
// the example: this tool's whole point is catching exactly this.
EXAMPLE_GEOJSON = JSON.stringify({
  type: "FeatureCollection",
  features: [{
    type: "Feature",
    properties: { name: "mismatched-example" },
    geometry: {
      type: "Polygon",
      coordinates: [[[1390000, 5140000], [1391000, 5140000], [1391000, 5141000], [1390000, 5141000], [1390000, 5140000]]]
    }
  }]
})
```

```{.webgeods-python #crs-inspect-py}
#| package: geopandas, shapely
import geopandas as gpd

EMPTY_FC = {"type": "FeatureCollection", "features": []}

gdf = None
for path in ["/uploaded.geojson", "/uploaded.shp", "/vsizip//uploaded.zip"]:
    try:
        gdf = gpd.read_file(path)
        break
    except Exception:
        pass

crs_warning = None
mismatch_warning = None
original_crs = None
is_geographic = None
bounds = None

if gdf is not None:
    if "name" not in gdf.columns:
        gdf["name"] = [f"geometry {i+1}" for i in range(len(gdf))]

    # A missing CRS is corrected (assumed WGS84, flagged) — but the
    # heuristic below cares about what the file DECLARES, so this has
    # to happen before reading original_crs, not after.
    if gdf.crs is None:
        gdf = gdf.set_crs("EPSG:4326")
        crs_warning = "No CRS found in the file — assuming WGS84 (EPSG:4326)."

    original_crs = gdf.crs
    is_geographic = bool(original_crs.is_geographic)
    bounds = [round(float(b), 6) for b in gdf.total_bounds] if len(gdf) > 0 else None

    # The actual differentiator: not just "what CRS does this file
    # claim", but "do the coordinates themselves agree with that
    # claim". A geographic CRS (degrees) whose bounds fall miles
    # outside -180..180 / -90..90 almost certainly isn't really
    # geographic — probably a projected file with a wrong/default CRS
    # label. The reverse (projected CRS, but the numbers already look
    # like plain lon/lat) is the same mistake in the other direction.
    if bounds is not None:
        looks_geographic = (
            -180 <= bounds[0] <= 180 and -180 <= bounds[2] <= 180 and
            -90 <= bounds[1] <= 90 and -90 <= bounds[3] <= 90
        )
        if is_geographic and not looks_geographic:
            mismatch_warning = (
                f"The CRS is declared as geographic ({original_crs.name}), but "
                f"the coordinates (roughly {bounds[0]:.1f} to {bounds[2]:.1f}, "
                f"{bounds[1]:.1f} to {bounds[3]:.1f}) fall far outside the "
                "range longitude/latitude allows (-180..180, -90..90). This "
                "file is very likely actually in a projected CRS, mislabeled."
            )
        elif not is_geographic and looks_geographic:
            mismatch_warning = (
                f"The CRS is declared as projected ({original_crs.name}), but "
                "the coordinates already look like plain longitude/latitude. "
                "This file is very likely actually in a geographic CRS "
                "(probably WGS84), mislabeled."
            )

    # MapLibre/GeoJSON require WGS84 — the summary above stays in the
    # file's own native CRS on purpose (that mismatch IS the point of
    # this tool), so the map gets its own throwaway reprojected copy
    # instead of reusing gdf directly. original_crs is never None
    # here (a missing CRS was already assumed WGS84 above).
    map_gdf = gdf if original_crs == "EPSG:4326" else gdf.to_crs("EPSG:4326")

    for col in gdf.columns:
        if col != "geometry":
            gdf[col] = gdf[col].fillna("")

{
    "mapFeatures": map_gdf.__geo_interface__ if gdf is not None else EMPTY_FC,
    "summary": {
        "total": len(gdf) if gdf is not None else 0,
        "crs": original_crs.to_string() if original_crs is not None else None,
        "crsName": original_crs.name if original_crs is not None else None,
        "isGeographic": is_geographic,
        "bounds": bounds,
        "crsWarning": crs_warning,
        "mismatchWarning": mismatch_warning
    }
}
```

targetCrsControl = {

  input.type = "text";
  input.id = "target-crs-input";

```{.webgeods-python #crs-convert-py}
#| inject: [targetCrs, uploadKindPy]
# Only run on demand (see convertButton below). Reprojects the CURRENT
# gdf (still in its own original CRS — crs-inspect-py above never
# modifies gdf itself, only the throwaway map_gdf copy) to whatever
# EPSG code the user typed, then returns it the same way
# geometry-export-shp-py does in the Validator: as an actual shapefile
# if the upload was one, zipped and base64-encoded, or as plain
# GeoJSON otherwise.
import base64
import io
import os
import zipfile

target = f"EPSG:{str(targetCrs).strip().replace('EPSG:', '').replace('epsg:', '')}"
converted = gdf.to_crs(target)

# Assigned to a variable, then returned as its own bare final line —
# a dict literal as the last line of an if/else branch does NOT become
# the cell's return value (Pyodide only auto-captures a bare top-level
# expression statement, and an if/else is a single compound statement,
# not one — verified empirically: the cell ran fine but its own
# .value came back undefined).
if uploadKindPy == "shapefile":
    converted.to_file("/tmp/webgeods_crs_export.shp", driver="ESRI Shapefile")
    buf = io.BytesIO()
    with zipfile.ZipFile(buf, "w", zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as z:
        for fname in sorted(os.listdir("/tmp")):
            if fname.startswith("webgeods_crs_export."):
                with open(f"/tmp/{fname}", "rb") as f:
                    z.writestr(fname.replace("webgeods_crs_export", "result"), f.read())
    result = {"kind": "shapefile", "data": base64.b64encode(buf.getvalue()).decode("ascii")}
else:
    result = {"kind": "geojson", "data": converted.__geo_interface__}

result
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| output: false
// base64 -> raw bytes, for the convert cell's shapefile branch
// (binary data can only cross the Pyodide->JS bridge as a cell value
// via a text encoding — same reasoning as
// geojson-shapefile-validator.qmd's base64ToBytes).
base64ToBytes = (base64Str) => {
  const binary = atob(base64Str);
  const bytes = new Uint8Array(binary.length);
  for (let i = 0; i < binary.length; i++) bytes[i] = binary.charCodeAt(i);
  return bytes;
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| output: false
// "shapefile", not "zip" too: unlike download in the Validator/other
// tools (mirroring the ORIGINAL upload format), a CRS conversion's
// output format is a free choice independent of how the file was
// selected — a zip-selected shapefile and an shp/dbf/shx-selected one
// both convert to the same thing here, a single re-zipped shapefile,
// which is why crs-convert-py's own `uploadKindPy` check only tests
// for "shapefile" contains both cases (see the assignment below).
convertButton = {
  const button = document.createElement("button");
  button.className = "webgeods-panel-btn";
  button.textContent = "⇄ Convert & Download";
  button.disabled = !inspectSummary || inspectSummary.total === 0;
  button.onclick = async () => {
    button.disabled = true;
    const originalText = button.textContent;
    button.textContent = "⌛ Converting...";
    try {
      window.targetCrs = document.getElementById("target-crs-input").value;
      window.uploadKindPy = (uploadKind === "zip" || uploadKind === "shapefile") ? "shapefile" : "geojson";
      await window.WebGeoDS.CodeCell.find("crs-convert-py").run();
      const result = document.getElementById("crs-convert-py").value;
      const base = WebGeoDS.Upload.baseName(uploadedFiles);
      const epsg = window.targetCrs.replace(/[^0-9]/g, "") || "converted";
      const options = { tool: "crs-inspector" };
      if (result.kind === "shapefile") {
        WebGeoDS.downloadBlob(base64ToBytes(result.data), base ? `${base}-epsg${epsg}.zip` : `converted-epsg${epsg}.zip`, "application/zip", options);
      } else {
        WebGeoDS.downloadBlob(JSON.stringify(result.data, null, 2), base ? `${base}-epsg${epsg}.geojson` : `converted-epsg${epsg}.geojson`, "application/geo+json", options);
      }
    } finally {
      button.disabled = false;
      button.textContent = originalText;
    }
  };
  return button;
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// Physically positioned here, between the panel and the map, matching
// the GeoSpatial File Inspector's own layout (a summary card is more
// useful read before the map than after it). The mismatch warning, if
// any, gets its own visually distinct row instead of being folded
// into a regular stat — it's the reason this tool exists.
statCard = {
  const s = inspectSummary;
  const box = document.createElement("div");
  box.className = "webgeods-stat-grid";

  const row = (label, value) => {
    const dt = document.createElement("div");
    dt.className = "webgeods-stat-label";
    dt.textContent = label;
    const dd = document.createElement("div");
    dd.className = "webgeods-stat-value";
    dd.textContent = value;
    box.append(dt, dd);
  };

  if (!s || s.total === 0) {
    row("Features", "0");
    row("—", "Upload a file or load the example above");
    return box;
  }

  row("Features", s.total.toLocaleString());
  row("CRS", s.crsWarning ? `${s.crs} ⚠️ ${s.crsWarning}` : (s.crs ?? "Unknown"));
  row("Type", s.isGeographic ? "Geographic (degrees)" : "Projected (usually meters)");
  row("Bounds", s.bounds ? s.bounds.join(", ") : "—");
  if (s.mismatchWarning) {
    row("⚠️ Mismatch", s.mismatchWarning);
  } else {
    row("Mismatch check", "✓ CRS and coordinates agree");
  }

  return box;
}
```
